sourceTitle: The AI Boom Is Testing America’s Power Grid
linkedinPost:
Your AI roadmap might be bottlenecked by a transformer — the electrical kind.

Knowledge at Wharton highlights a growing constraint: the grid. AI’s power appetite is colliding with real-world permitting, interconnect queues, and transmission limits. Fancy roadmaps won’t matter if you can’t plug them in.

From the front lines, here’s what separates programs that scale from those that stall:

- Sequence use cases by compute intensity. Don’t lead with GPU-hungry science projects if your power contract renews next quarter.
- Make energy a KPI. Track tokens per kWh, throughput per watt, and cost per successful task — not just latency.
- Co-design with facilities. Capacity planning, heat, and siting are now product decisions.
- Build reversible ops. Use burstable workloads, demand-response windows, and multi-region flexibility so you’re not hostage to one substation.
- Talk to your utility early. The teams that treat utilities as strategic partners, not vendors, win time.

My take: AI strategy just became an infrastructure strategy. If your CFO and facilities lead aren’t in the same room as your AI team, you’re not doing portfolio planning — you’re gambling.

How are you derisking power in your 2026 AI plan? #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI #AIStrategy
